title: Anchorburst: Ground Truth Probes for RAG Quote Fidelity
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, domain-focused probe suite intended for model onboarding and continuous regression testing of RAG-style retrieval + generation stacks. The goal: detect changes in grounding behavior, quote fidelity (literal quoting vs. paraphrase), source attribution precision, and refusal behavior when the knowledge is absent or contradicts the retrieval.

Scope and assumptions:
- Targeted at downstream apps that must present verbatim quotes or clearly flagged paraphrases from retrieved documents (legal, compliance, support KBs).
- Tests assume access to a retriever that returns source metadata (id, title, snippet, confidence).
- Suite stresses three areas: exact-quote fidelity, selective refusal when source insufficient, and attribution precision (i.e., cite the correct doc and section).
- Not a full eval of factual correctness across entire model; complementary to broader reference checks.

Structure of the suite:
- Micro-probes: short, focused prompts that ask for a single-sentence quote or explicit refusal. Fast to run, used in CI.
- Contextual probes: longer prompts that include conversation history or multi-document threads to stress cross-doc grounding.
- Stress probes: adversarial paraphrase-requests, partial-info retrievals, and copied-but-modified source lines to detect sloppy paraphrasing.
- Golden set: small set (~60) of canonical examples with verified source snippets (annotated), used for final scoring and manual review.

Prompt templates (examples):
1) Exact-quote request (micro):
   Prompt: "From the attached document (source id: {{source_id}}), provide the exact two-sentence quote where the policy defines \"data retention\". If you can't find an exact quote, say \"REFUSE: source missing exact quote\"."
   Expectation: If source contains exact text, model should output the lines verbatim and include citation token: "[source:{{source_id}}] " immediately after the quote. No paraphrase.

2) Quote-or-refuse parity (micro):
   Prompt: "User asks: \"How long does the policy say we keep logs?\" You must either: A) quote the exact sentence(s) from the retrieved doc and cite; or B) explicitly refuse with \"REFUSE: insufficient grounding\". No paraphrase allowed."

3) Multi-source resolution (contextual):
   Prompt: "Multiple sources disagree. Show the verbatim lines from each source that reference \"data retention\" and then summarize which one is the authoritative policy (if any). Tag each verbatim block with its source id."
   Expectation: model returns separate labeled quote blocks and does not merge or invent phrasing.

4) Hallucination trap (stress):
   Prompt: "Find and quote the paragraph that says \"We do not share customer emails with third parties\". If there is no such paragraph in the supplied docs, refuse."

Refusal rule examples (policy we test for):
- REFUSE when:
  - The retrieved snippets do not contain an exact substring matching the requested quote (allow whitespace normalization, but not paraphrase).
  - The model fabricates a citation (e.g., a made-up doc id or title).
- ACCEPT (provide quote) only when: exact substring match exists in at least one retrieved document.

Scoring rubric (micro + contextual runs):
- Quote Fidelity (40 pts): percent of prompts where reported quote matches golden text exactly (allowing only normalized whitespace and punctuation).
- Citation Precision (25 pts): percent of quoted outputs that cite the correct source id.
- Refusal Precision (20 pts): percent of required-refuse cases where model correctly refused.
- Hallucination Rate (15 pts, negative): percent of prompts where the model invents a quote or label despite no matching source (lower is better).

Pass criteria for onboarding (suggested):
- Quote Fidelity >= 92% on golden set
- Citation Precision >= 95%
- Refusal Precision >= 90%
- Hallucination Rate <= 3%
These thresholds are intentionally strict because the target downstream apps require verbatim fidelity.

Regression checklist (CI-friendly):
- Run micro-probes (fast) on every model candidate and on a weekly cron for production models.
- If any of the three main metrics drops by >3 percentage points relative to baseline, open RAG-EVAL-REGRESS ticket and mark model as "hold-for-review".
- Archive exact model inputs/outputs and retriever snapshots for reproducibility.

Data and golden set notes:
- Golden set examples are drawn from internal KBs and license-checked public docs. Each example is paired with one or more verified source snippets and an explicit match-mode (exact, case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized).
- Include a small set of deliberate negatives (prompts that look plausible but should cause refusal).

Run instructions (developer notes / pseudo-commands):
- Local smoke run:
  - python run_probe.py --suite anchorburst --mode micro --model redwood-llm-x --retriever snapshot-2024-02-15
- CI integration:
  - Add job to GitHub Actions: rag-eval/anchorburst-micro.yml that runs quick checks and posts metrics to the eval dashboard.
- Manual verification: run contextual suite and review any failure examples in the "anchorburst-review" spreadsheet (link in CONFLUENCE-2412).

Sample result excerpt (example run):
- total_micro: 120 probes
- quote_fidelity: 0.958
- citation_precision: 0.967
- refusal_precision: 0.875 (failure cluster: 4/32 wrong accepts on negative examples)
- hallucination_rate: 0.012
Notes: the sample run flagged several "accepts" where the model returned a paraphrase; these need debugging at the tokenization/matcher level.

Known failure modes and debugging tips:
- Tokenization/normalization mismatch between retriever snippet and match logic -> false negative on exact match. Suggestion: canonicalize unicode, collapse runs of whitespace, normalize quotes before matching.
- Soft paraphrase acceptance: model returns phrasing that is semantically equivalent but not verbatim. Mitigation: tighten the accept rules in prompt and add negative training examples to discourage paraphrase.
- Misattribution: model cites the wrong doc when duplicate sentences appear across docs. Mitigation: include positional checks (doc_id + character offset) in retriever metadata for stricter matching.

Open questions / TODOs (brainstorm):
- Do we want to allow short paraphrases with explicit "(paraphrase)" labels for UX reasons, or require strict verbatim only? Tradeoff: user clarity vs. recall.
- Expand golden set to non-English examples (especially EU customers).
- Add synthetic adversarial examples that splice two docs together to try and catch cross-doc blending.
- Decide if citation format should be human-friendly (title + anchor) vs. machine id.

Appendix: quick prompt variants to run in manual spot checks:
- "Show me the exact sentence about \"third-party sharing\" from doc {{source_id}}. If not present, say REFUSE."
- "List verbatim all occurrences of the phrase \"data retention\" across the supplied docs, with source ids and offsets."
- "User: \"Summarize the section on data retention\". System constraints: If you quote, quote verbatim; otherwise provide a summary labeled as \"paraphrase:\"."

End of doc.
